title: PACKET_DESCRIBE copies a NetScaler record out of the page buffer using a length taken straight from the file
object: nstrace_buf, one g_malloc(NSPR_PAGESIZE) page buffer of 8192 bytes
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the page buffer is alive throughout. This corpus's rows are spatial by construction.
shape: a record size read from the file makes the copy start inside the page buffer and run past its end
allocator_layer: the system allocator itself: one g_malloc, no inner layer. wiretap does not use wmem, which is what makes this the NOT-NESTED spatial row for tshark.
fidelity: real allocator, model consumer. The allocation is the upstream size (NSPR_PAGESIZE = 8192, wiretap/netscaler.c:52, unchanged at the pin) and the length is the upstream field's full range. GLib is not linked: g_malloc is malloc plus abort-on-failure and g_free is free, which is all this case uses of it. The copy is REDUCED TO ITS FIRST CROSSING BYTE -- the unreduced memcpy spans 65471 bytes past the allocation, and walking all of it would be an unbounded read through whatever follows; the magnitude is reported as extent= and stated in PROVENANCE.md. The fix adds three guards; the case is reduced to the one that bounds the copy.
live_proof: the fix is an ancestor of v4.6.8 and the pin carries its guards: v4.6.8:wiretap/netscaler.c contains 2 occurrences of "record crosses page boundary", and the page buffer is still g_malloc(NSPR_PAGESIZE) at :731. The parent 19c51d27b9^ has the allocation at :682 and no guard at all. The case reconstructs the pre-fix consumer shape against the shipped allocator, the convention at ../../memcached/allocator-repros/README.md:132-135.
distinguishing: the arms differ by ONE guard -- whether the remaining room in the page is compared with the record size. The allocation, the offset and the record size are identical in both.

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm reports cap=8192 touched=73663 extent=65471 crossed=1 damage=1; the fixed arm crossed=0 damage=0 with the same cap, touched and extent, because the guard refuses the record rather than changing its size. MEASURED 2026-10-06, results/20261006-native-plain-heap/.

native-detect.oracle: ASan REPORTS. The crossing leaves the malloc bound, so a redzone sits exactly where it lands. MEASURED two-sided 2026-10-06 -- buggy 'heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 1 ... 0 bytes after 8192-byte region', attributed to the labelled read_probe (shared/corpus.h:64) with the allocation at case.c:28; fixed arm silent, exit 0. The wmem and sub-object corpora record the opposite reading for the opposite reason.

spatial.oracle: PREDICTED: faults at the labelled probe. The crossing leaves the g_malloc bound, which per-object bounds enforce, so the bounds-only arm must catch it. The corresponding malloc-granular reading already exists in the tshark app port: fixtures fx2 and fx3 read level0 RETURN and shrink FAULT oob there. NOT YET MEASURED as a corpus case -- this corpus has no capstone-domain runner.

sublet.oracle: PREDICTED: faults, identically to the spatial arm. Sublet is revocation and has nothing to fire on while the page buffer is alive; the catch is the inherited per-object bound. NOT YET MEASURED as a corpus case.

sublet-chunks.oracle: PREDICTED: faults, and for the SAME reason as the spatial arm rather than a different one. The chunk port narrows wmem chunks, and wiretap's page buffer is not a wmem chunk -- it is a direct g_malloc -- so the port changes nothing here. That is the point of the row: it is the one tshark case the inner-allocator port is irrelevant to. NOT YET MEASURED.

poisoncap-spatial.oracle: PREDICTED and UNMEASURABLE HERE: mode 0 bounds each allocation, so it catches a crossing of the malloc bound.
poisoncap-spatial.note: UNMEASURABLE ON THIS HOST at the time of writing, checked rather than assumed: ports/common/cmake/toolchains/cheribsd.cmake:4-9 requires CHERI_SDK and CHERI_SYSROOT and FATAL_ERRORs without them, and no SDK, purecap sysroot or image existed here.

poisoncap-protected.oracle: PREDICTED and UNMEASURABLE HERE: mode 1 adds temporal protection to the same bounds, so it catches the crossing for the mode-0 reason.
poisoncap-protected.note: UNMEASURABLE ON THIS HOST at the time of writing, same check as the arm above.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-06 on this host: CAUGHT. signal=34 (SIGPROT), **si_code=1**, addr=pc=0x102006, and SUPERVISE resolved 'expect read_probe 0x102006' independently -- so the fault is AT the labelled probe and SCHEMA rule 2 is met for this row. The crossing is 65471 bytes past a g_malloc(8192), whose capability is exactly 8192 long (measured), so it leaves the allocation by far more than any size-class slack. the platform's own bounds control fired in the same boot: cheribsd-bounds runs abi-probe oob, which sets bounds to exactly 16 and reads offset 16, and it PASSED alongside cheribsd-abi reporting CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1. A spatial completion is therefore a reading, not a silent detector. si_code 1 is the BOUNDS code; every runner in this tree hardcodes PROT_CHERI_TAG=2, which is the TAG code, and the bounds code was not recorded anywhere before this run. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-07 by the committed runner, results/20261007-cheribsd/: CAUGHT. signal=34 (SIGPROT), si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), addr=pc=0x1023c4, and supervise resolved `expect wsh_read_probe 0x1023b4` from the ELF independently of the run. The fault lies INSIDE the labelled probe, whose extent is [0x1023b4, 0x1023d0) (size 0x1c) -- the offset is the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion, not equality with the symbol address. The crossing is 65471 bytes past a g_malloc(8192), and 8192 is exactly a size class, so it leaves the USABLE allocation by far more than any slack could absorb. ATTRIBUTION IS NOW ESTABLISHED, which it was not before. This corpus declared its probe `static` in shared/corpus.h until 2026-10-07, so every translation unit had a private copy and supervise reported the symbol unavailable -- the reason this row read 'attribution: not established'. The probe is now DECLARED in the header and DEFINED ONCE in shared/driver.c. Proven inert: the native runner was re-run afterwards and its verdict summary is unchanged (plain=reproduced, asan-buggy=heap-buffer-overflow, asan-fixed=silent). The platform controls fired in the same boot: cheribsd-abi reported `CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1` and cheribsd-bounds reported CHERI_BOUNDARY_READY, both PASS, and the committed runner refuses to report a suite whose controls did not fire (exit 75) rather than letting an empty boot read as a result.
